history.summary: Encrypted webhooks.secret at rest with internal/credentials (AES-256-GCM, AAD bound to the immutable webhook ID), removed all API/frontend plaintext exposure, implemented the confirmed absent/null=preserve, empty=clear, non-empty=replace tri-state, added paired SQLite/MySQL schema migrations plus offline --migrate-webhook-secrets/--rollback-webhook-secrets actions, moved decryption to the HMAC delivery boundary with zero-outbound-on-credential-failure, and along the way fixed two pre-existing IMAP/SMTP test fragilities (fixed-count goose.Down assumptions) that the new migration exposed. Full local gates, real MySQL, real-backend browser coverage, and the production-image webhook container lifecycle all pass; docs, self-review, and a backlog issue for webhook URL secrets are included.

All acceptance criteria verified with comprehensive evidence: cryptographic boundary intact (shared keyring, ID-bound AAD, record-copy failure), transaction safety proven (read-back verification, plaintext-insert trigger test, concurrent-mutation detection), API isolation verified (tri-state decoder, write-only responses, PermissionModifySystem enforcement), frontend never leaks secrets (no prefill, explicit controls, browser test confirmation), zero-outbound guarantee tested (credential failures excluded before http.Client.Do, multiple failure modes covered), lifecycle operations complete (migration idempotence, rollback atomicity, schema Down guarded), comprehensive test coverage (764+ new lines, SQLite/MySQL/API/browser/Docker verified), documentation thorough (threat model, matrices, prerequisites, key loss handling). IMAP/SMTP regression fixed (goose.DownTo instead of assumed version). No issues requiring fixes.
NULL legacy secret rows can report successful metadata updates without changing the row, and rollback rejects valid NULL+ciphertext states.

Made runtime and rollback predicates NULL-aware, added exact in-transaction verification of metadata and concrete credential storage, proved NULL preserve/clear/replace/deactivation/migration/rollback/no-op/conflict behavior on SQLite and real MySQL, and broadened CI to run every MySQL webhook credential test. Full verification, browser, Docker lifecycle, fuzzing, dependency audits, and security scanners completed without a new finding.

Security finding resolved: NULL legacy secrets now handled identically to empty strings in all predicates (PostWebhook, PutWebhook, rollback); full-row storage verification with metadata fields ensures metadata-bundled updates persist and are observable in delivery selection; MySQL changed-row semantics handled correctly; all valid/ambiguous/concurrent states tested on SQLite and real MySQL 8.4.11; 6 comprehensive test functions prove preserve/clear/replace/deactivate/no-op/concurrent/rollback behavior; CI broadened to run all MySQL webhook credential tests. No issues requiring fixes; all iteration-1 acceptance criteria remain satisfied.
Independent specialist re-review confirmed the NULL data-integrity finding closed and found no remaining high-confidence security issue.
Final complete-diff review found no high-confidence correctness, security, migration, concurrency, or compatibility defect.
